narrative.overview:
Learning Compass should feel like a well-prepared study desk at home: every tool has a clear place, the page is quiet enough to concentrate, and the next useful action is easy to find. The interface is calm, clear, encouraging, and structured. It supports a child working at arm's length on a desktop or tablet without adopting an infantile or entertainment-first tone.

The visual system uses a soft sky field to hold white study surfaces, deep blue to signal direction, and semantic green, amber, and red only when learning evidence calls for them. Density is comfortable rather than sparse: information is grouped into compact cards, but generous type sizes and consistent gaps keep the work legible.

Avoid flashy gamification, neon palettes, excessive cartoon decoration, and the compressed feel of an administration dashboard.
keyCharacteristics: Soft sky background with clean paper-like working surfaces.
Strong, rare blue states that make the active path unmistakable.
Large system typography designed for reading at arm's length.
Thin structural borders, restrained ambient shadows, and predictable rounded geometry.
Semantic feedback that is supportive and never relies on colour alone.

rules.name: The Compass Blue Is Direction Rule
rules.body: Use deep blue for the active path and the most important action, not as decoration across every card.

rules.name: The Evidence Colour Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red must describe a real learning state and must always be paired with text, an icon, or another non-colour cue.

rules.name: The Quiet Field Rule
rules.body: Keep the sky canvas visible around white working surfaces; do not flood entire screens with saturated colour.

rules.name: The Read at Arm's Length Rule
rules.body: Learner-facing instructions stay at 17px or larger; reserve 12–15px text for metadata, chips, and supporting status only.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Use the system sans stack across learning surfaces so bilingual text remains coherent; monospace is limited to technical keys or machine-readable values.

rules.name: The One Reading Axis Rule
rules.body: On narrow screens, preserve a clear vertical learning sequence. Horizontal scrolling is acceptable for navigation and oversized diagrams, not for ordinary lesson content.

rules.name: The Comfortable Grid Rule
rules.body: Prefer a partially filled final row over stretching cards into unusually wide reading blocks.

rules.name: The Flat by Default Rule
rules.body: Cards and inputs rest without shadows; add elevation only to communicate shell hierarchy, selection, or hover response.

rules.name: The Blue Ambient Rule
rules.body: Shadows use low-opacity Compass Blue rather than neutral black so depth remains gentle on the sky canvas.

rules.name: The Radius Has Rank Rule
rules.body: Larger containers receive larger corners; do not apply pill geometry to cards or rectangular navigation items.

dos: Do keep the Quiet Sky canvas visible around Paper White working surfaces.
Do make one active route or next action unmistakable with Compass Blue.
Do preserve 17–18px learner-facing text and generous line-height for explanations.
Do use thin borders and restrained spacing to organise dense learning content.
Do pair semantic colours with words, icons, or status labels.
Do collapse multi-column learning layouts into one clear reading axis on narrow screens.
donts: Don't introduce neon colours, glossy gradients, confetti-like decoration, or game-economy visuals.
Don't fill every card or button with Compass Blue; its rarity gives it directional authority.
Don't add heavy black shadows or elevate every surface.
Don't shrink learner instructions to dashboard-sized metadata text.
Don't rely on red or green alone to communicate an answer state.
Don't turn the interface into a dense administration dashboard or an overly childish cartoon world.
